subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose an opt-in cap only for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but current node-host behavior intentionally relies on unlimited reconnect recovery, so the permanent retry contract is a product and compatibility decision rather than a purely mechanical fix.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep node-host unlimited by default, add a package-level cap option, and wire it only into maintainer-approved short-lived clients with proof for both capped and default behavior.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Make every GatewayClient stop after a fixed number of attempts, accepting the risk that long-lived node hosts no longer recover automatically after extended outages.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Treat unlimited reconnects as by design and close the issue only if maintainers accept the resource-risk tradeoff and document the intended recovery model.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep node-host unlimited by default, add a package-level cap option, and wire it only into maintainer-approved short-lived clients with proof for both capped and default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The original Gateway WebSocket control-plane work and much of the gateway-client policy history trace through this owner path.
